subject: AI & Agents
title: Auditing AI Systems
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Auditing AI Systems.

hook.text: We audit financial systems annually. Why don't we audit AI systems the same way?

buildup.text: AI audits test systems for bias, accuracy, security, and compliance with regulations.

discovery.text: Third-party auditors can probe models with test cases designed to expose failure modes.

twist.text: Many companies resist audits, claiming models are proprietary trade secrets.

climax.text: New York City passed a law requiring audits of AI hiring tools. Others may follow.

punchline.text: Trust but verify — especially when the decision-maker is a machine.

quiz.question: What do AI audits test for?
options: Bias, accuracy, security, and regulatory compliance

details.summary: AI auditing evaluates systems for bias, accuracy, security, and compliance. Independent audits help ensure AI behaves as intended and meets ethical standards before and after deployment.
details.whyItMatters: Without audits, AI systems operate as black boxes with unchecked power over consequential decisions. Regular independent auditing builds trust and catches problems early.
takeaways: AI audits check for bias, accuracy, and regulatory compliance
Independent auditing increases transparency and public trust
The EU AI Act requires audits for high-risk AI systems

faq.question: What does an AI audit typically examine?
faq.answer: Auditors evaluate training data for bias, test model accuracy across different groups, review security practices, check regulatory compliance, and assess whether the system performs as claimed.

faq.question: Are AI audits required by law?
faq.answer: Increasingly yes. The EU AI Act mandates audits for high-risk systems. New York City requires bias audits for AI used in hiring. More jurisdictions are following with similar requirements.
